newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open 0.05 cent lower.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open unchanged to 0.05 cent per lb lower on Thursday, as the market is expected to consolidate recent gains, dealers said.
Prices climbed to new contract highs for the third consecutive session on Wednesday amid brisk fund buying, but ended the day only slightly firmer.

July closed 0.03 cent a lb higher to 11.51 cents per lb, having traded from 11.34 to 11.58 cents, a new contract high. October ended up 0.03 cent at 11.32, while the deferred contracts finished 0.06 and 0.04 cent firmer.
An estimated 33,315 lots changed hands on the day.
Trading sources said the market would find resistance at each point higher, while chart resistance was pegged at 11.65-11.70 cents in July, a high from late April.
Support was seen from 11.20 to 11.00 cents.

In London, white sugar futures eased early Wednesday, as the market continued to retrace recent gains. At 0838 EDT/1238 GMT, LIFFE spot August contract was down $1.10 at $327.30, and the rest of the board was $1.40 to $0.40 lower.
